name: Apomorphine
description: Dopamine agonist small molecule that stimulates the brain’s dopamine receptors

note.text: Uprima, Ixense and Taluvian were authorised EU-wide in 2001; all were withdrawn or expired by 2006 for commercial reasons.

bullets: **Binds dopamine receptors:** strongly D4; moderately D2, D3, D5 (label)
**For ED,** studied as a drug acting in the brain, not on penile vessels
**Sexual stimulation** was needed for Uprima to work (EMA)

practical.routes: Under-skin injection or infusion; under the tongue in ED trials
practical.pharmacokinetics: Peak in 10 to 60 minutes; human metabolism route not known
practical.soldAs: Prescription injection and infusion (Apokyn, Onapgo, generics)
practical.monitored: Blood pressure, sleepiness, QT interval, nausea

regulatory.text: Approved for Parkinson’s (2004); never for ED
ED approvals (2001) withdrawn or expired by 2006

references: Guillén et al., Arch Sex Behav, sublingual apomorphine for ED review, Nov 2020
EMA, Uprima public assessment record, May 2006
